l4Discriminating.text: Synthetic data generation process outside physical apparatus — The datastreams do not originate from real physical sensors in Meridian, but are generated by an external simulation, synthetic harness, or automated testing script. A digital generator operating on numerical arrays would trivially apply a uniform 1.50 multiplier to observatory variables while neglecting dimensional reciprocity, and could reuse a shared pseudo-random noise sequence or buffer array between pendulum_lab and resonator_obs with a 3-day offset, explaining why r has reached an extraordinary 0.909.

l4Discriminating.text: Synthetic data generation process outside Meridian's physical apparatus — The records may not reflect physical instruments at all, but rather synthetic numerical output produced by an external software script, simulation, or automated test suite. A computational generator would easily apply an arbitrary scalar (1.500) to 'observatory' variables without physical dimensional consistency, and reuse a pseudo-random sequence with a 3-day index shift between pendulum_lab and resonator_obs. With r reaching 0.948 across 122 points, the relationship is virtually deterministic, pointing toward an algorithmic generator rather than noisy physical reality.
